subject: SOC 2 recertification & renewal — evidence plan + capacity increase
messages:

Cc: security@tremont.tech
Date: 2028-06-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 recert timeline + renewal amendment (year 3)

Hi Olga,

As we approach the end of year two, our security team asked for a quick sync on Tremont's SOC 2 recertification timeline and how that will impact our renewal. Two asks from us: 1) a clear evidence handoff plan (we have a narrower window this year) and 2) confirmation of the retention window for audit logs — we may need an extra 90 days of indexed logs for a forensic spot check.

Separately, usage has risen faster than forecast and we're evaluating a 30% seat/throughput bump for Q3. Can you outline the process to add dedicated seats and whether that affects the recertification scope or timeline?

Attached an updated SOW draft (v2) and a quick inventory of the evidence we expect to share.

Thanks,
Amelia Brooks
Head of IT, Tremont Tech
amelia.brooks@tremont.tech

[attachment: tremont_sow_v2.pdf]

Cc: security@tremont.tech, karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-06-23T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 recert timeline + renewal amendment (year 3)

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. High level response here, will follow with a MAP (mutual action plan) by end of day tomorrow.

Quick answers:
- Evidence handoff: we can support a staged evidence upload cadence; preferred approach is a two-week inbound window per evidence category. We will provide a shared Drive folder plus an SFTP fallback.
- Retention: we can extend indexed audit-log retention by +90 days for the renewal term; this requires a contract amendment to the retention SLA (small monthly delta).
- Capacity/seat increase: 30% throughput bump is feasible. If you want Dedicated pool capacity added to your Dedicated environment, we need a confirmed seat/throughput target and a 30-day lead time for GPU allocation. Seat-only (console access) increases can be immediate.

I've looped in Karthik (security ops) to scope any evidence-parsing work and Ben (AM) to confirm commercial uplift and timing.

Next: Karthik will propose an evidence cadence and Ben will provide a contract redline and cost delta. Will put the MAP + DocuSign bundle in one doc.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Team — quick internal plan for Tremont:

1) Evidence cadence: propose 3 waves over 6 weeks: infra controls + IAM (wk1-2), logging/observability bundles (wk3-4), operational evidence (wk5-6). Each wave has a 10-business-day acceptance window.

2) Log retention change: storing an extra 90 days of indexed logs increases storage tier costs and the export cadence for their SIEM integrations. Commercial needs to capture a one-time reindex fee + monthly storage delta.

3) Capacity: to accommodate a 30% throughput bump we have two options: a) temporary burst nodes for 90 days (fast, slightly higher unit cost) or b) permanent Dedicated pool increase (30-day lead, better unit economics). Recommend offering both with pricing and letting the customer choose.

Action items:
- Ben to draft amendment language (retention SLA + seat/throughput options).
- Vanessa to size burst vs permanent pricing and confirm GPU availability window.
- Olga/Karthik to prepare the evidence inventory template and Drive/SFTP instructions.

I'll assemble the evidence checklist and upload the template to the shared drive by EOD.

—Karthik
Principal Security Engineer

Hi Amelia — attaching a redline and a short pricing summary for the two capacity options.

Summary:
- Retention amendment: +90 days indexed log retention, included as an addendum to the Master Services Agreement. Monthly delta: $2,400.
- Burst nodes (90d): one-time setup $1,200 + prorated usage.
- Permanent Dedicated pool increase (30%): estimated monthly delta $6,200; 30-day lead time required to provision.

Next steps: if you confirm which capacity option you prefer I'll queue the DocuSign amendment. If you want us to run a 30-day burst while the Dedicated pool is provisioned, we can include both in the same amendment.
